body.statement: For arbitrary \((H,t)\), the sharp pinned set is exactly \(\Theta_I(H,t)\), its support endpoints are the extrema over the feasible branch LPs, and branchwise primal--dual alternatives classify each requested pin system as infeasible, redundant, or jointly binding. In the family of thm:strict-support-relaxation-gap with \(R=2\), pinning \(\theta_1=s_1-a\) yields the sharp slice \(\theta_2\in[s_2-a,s_2-a/2]\), whereas slicing the outer set as in HuntingtonKlein2026, Definition 3 on p. 15, yields \(\theta_2\in[s_2-a,s_2]\); the requested-pin upper-endpoint gap is exactly \(a/2\).
body.justification: Pinning is the anchor paper's main device for interpreting joint heterogeneity, so its slices must share one attainable bias witness.
body.gap: HuntingtonKlein2026, Definition 3 on p. 15, slices the outer difference polytope and does not characterize simultaneous sharp pins or quantify their endpoint error.
body.consumer: The ACS returns-to-college analysis can distinguish an effect configuration ruled out by the common bias mechanism from one merely removed by a marginal pin.
